# nova-tools fixes

<!-- Generated from docs/fixes.sexp by tools/roadmap. Do not edit this file: edit docs/fixes.sexp and run `make roadmap`. -->

The point releases after v1.2.2: what each one shipped, is shipping or will ship. A point release carries fixes only; new work is in ROADMAP.md. nova-sprint's point releases are in that repository's FIXES.md.

## v1.2.3 (shipped, 2026-10-10)

The split: nova-sprint, nova-card and nova-work, with their models and docs, leave this repository for mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint.

- **The sprint tools leave nova-tools** (shipped). Their commands, packages, models and docs move to mas-bandwidth/nova-sprint, and CI refuses their paths here. From: the split, layers L5 to L7; PR #5591.

## v1.2.4 (shipped, 2026-10-10)

One fix: the sprint store's function library is back at its v1.2.2 digest, so an adopt can load it.

- **Six Lua comment lines restored** (shipped). The function library's digest is its v1.2.2 value again, so the adopt's shadow tick accepts it. From: PR #5592, head 7d1dc0c06.

## v1.2.5 (in-progress)

The roadmap and this page come back as data, and the open issues move into the roadmap.

- **ROADMAP.md and FIXES.md generated from s-expression data** (in-progress). docs/roadmap.sexp and docs/fixes.sexp are the data; `make roadmap` writes both pages, and a test fails when a page differs from what its data renders. From: PR #5533.

## v1.2.6 (planned)

The fixes held during the split, the point-release candidates found on 2026-10-10, the owed tests, and the sprint store cards that are point-release work. Each is re-applied or written in this repository, then cut as one release.

- **The card tells the child its wall: deadline and temporary directory** (in-progress). The worker card tells the child its deadline, and the native wall passes the slot temporary directory so TMPDIR is the slot one. From: nova-tools PR #5575, head 4725d7d7d; landed in dev as 7dc8304560 via PR #5594.
- **A reader writes its scratch inside its job** (in-progress). A reader's child is given a writable scratch directory inside its job: TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP name $JOB/tmp, made before the child starts and removed with the job, and the read brief says so. A write the wall refuses outside the job ends the read in the reader's own environment, not as a missing verdict, and the read is run once more on the same reader instead of spending it and sending the card to cannot ask. From: measured 2026-10-11 by the seat's inbox pass: reads returned no verdict because the reader wrote under /tmp and the card wall refused it.
- **A walled lane tokens are read where its harness writes them** (shipped). Walled sessions live under the wall home, tokens are read from there first, and a session in no database is unread rather than zero, so the token cap can trip. From: nova-tools PR #5590, head 0c4fd7ea; landed in dev as 1babe4a43f via PR #5595.
- **The hosted tests are green on main and nightly** (planned). Two hosted tests are red on main and nightly (the fork bomb wall cap and jobs as worktrees of one mirror); make them pass there. From: v1.2.5 candidate list.
- **A friend AI moved to another machine uses the provider key that worked** (in-progress). After a move the friend AI ran with a stored provider key that differs from the working one, and the provider refused it. The stored key is replaced by the owner, then the friend AI restarts through the play. From: v1.2.5 candidate list.
- **release build refuses to ship without the sprint release** (in-progress). nova-update release build without --sprint-release ships no sprint tools and succeeds; it refuses unless an explicit opt-out flag is given. From: nova-tools PR #5571 cold read.
- **The release changelog lists merge-queue merges** (in-progress). The cut changelog says no pull request merged since the previous tag although the merge queue merged many; the listing includes merge-queue merges. From: v1.2.4 cut note.
- **A child ended at its deadline with a commit and no result gets a report** (planned). The card already tells the child to finish at 80 percent of its wall; for a child that works on to the deadline anyway, the run now writes a RESULT.md naming the branch, the commit count and the head when the deadline ended it with commits in the repository and no report of its own. The report has no findings head, so it is never scored as the child's own work. From: fault 9, 2026-10-10.
- **Members are restarted and checked after adoption** (in-progress). After installing, the play restarts every member, reader and friend daemon whose binary it replaced, fails each running process that does not report the installed version, prints a refusal's cause whole, and ends with one table: host, version running, members and readers up, harness present, disk free. From: bug 13, fleet/tools.yml.
- **A draining member's beat carries this tick's no-room word** (in-progress). The member asks Room every tick before the drain return, so a member that drained under its disk floor stops saying no room once the disk is freed (nova-sprint tla/NoRoom.tla, WordIsThisTicks). From: v1.2.5 candidate 5; the PR #5569 follow-up.
- **A friend's lane runs only a card the server has taken for her** (in-progress). A free lane takes its card by id and starts nothing until the take is answered OK; a refused take (the machine STOPPED) is asked again on a later pass, a batch daemon takes her ready cards, and a card set aside on a refused take or finish is taken again (tla/FriendLaneTake.tla). From: a friend host, 2026-10-10 20:14Z: a one-shot friend's 23 lanes ran ready cards and set them aside.
- **The adopt removes the unit of a friend who moved hosts** (in-progress). The friends step of the tools play splits the stale friend daemons live lists by what launchd holds: it reinstalls the ones the host runs (the friends table's place for them) and removes the unit of a friend who no longer lives there (installed, not loaded) with nova-friend uninstall. From: dogfood 2026-10-10: stale friend unit on the seat host.
- **A friend's batch take names the epoch of her ready cards** (in-progress). The server refuses every worker verb that names no epoch; the batch take sent none, so a batch friend's ready cards were never taken. The take now names the newest epoch her row holds, and a lane's take names the epoch her row says for the card. From: a friend host, 2026-10-10 20:53Z: take REFUSED, a worker's verb names the epoch.
- **A friend's lane wall always has a coordinator self to deny** (in-progress). nova-friend install takes --deny-self and writes it into the agent, the seat play passes nova_friend_deny_self to a reinstall whose plist records none, and with no flag the daemon denies the seat's working root, so no lane exits 125 with bad_profile for a missing deny list. From: a one-shot friend host, 2026-10-10: every lane exit 125, the daemon ran with no --deny-self.
- **A fleet loops play refuses when its checkout version differs from the adopted release** (planned). Fleet plays run only from the checkout of the adopted release, and refuse when the checkout's version differs from the release installed on the host. From: dogfood 2026-10-10 evening: fleet-only restart.
- **A friend's lanes are thin clients of the sprint server** (in-progress). Each lane asks the server what it holds (take --lane), runs exactly that, and reports by the ids, epoch and lane the server gave; a refusal drops the job and the lane asks again. lanes.json keeps sessions and owed stop-returns only, never what a lane holds, and reads go through the same lane loop. The model is tla/FriendLane.tla. From: a one-shot friend host, 2026-10-10: took logged while the server showed the card ready, and progress sent at epoch 0.
- **A friend's lane wall reads the pinned harness it runs** (shipped). nova-friend install takes --wall-reads and writes it into the agent, and the seat play passes nova_friend_wall_reads to a reinstall whose plist records none, so a pinned harness whose shim execs a directory under the home no longer exits 126 (Operation not permitted) for every lane. From: a one-shot friend host, 2026-10-10: every lane exit 126 after the harness pin; the wall denied reading the pinned harness directory.
- **A friend's new epoch retires her older-epoch items and starts empty** (in-progress). On the sprint's new epoch the daemon moves every older-epoch inbox and outbox item to the retired folder named for its epoch, kept, never deleted, and the live folders start the new epoch empty; on the same signal the lanes forget their sessions and the present is owed, so a full or stale session never carries across a clear. From: the seat ledger v1.2.4-held-2026-10-10.md friend snap, 2026-10-10: 323 inbox items and 535 outbox REPORTs of epoch 15, each refused (not on her row).
- **A friend's lane session full or missing starts a fresh one itself** (in-progress). A provider's context-limit refusal on a lane's session, or a session the harness no longer has, no longer counts the card's turns against it and waits for a hand session plus a restart: the lane starts a fresh session itself, seeded from the friend's own files, its card continues in it (once per card; after that the refusal is the card's business again), and the seat is told once per renewal. From: the owner 2026-10-10: what else is manual that should be automatic from the machine.
- **The worker brief says never amend, rebase or reset onto origin** (planned). The child rule no-rewrite-history in fleet/child-rules.txt, byte for byte the copy nova-sprint embeds (its add refuses a held rules file that differs), stops children rewriting history, which caused the does-not-descend refusals. A test pins the file's digest in both repositories. From: v1.2.5 candidate list.
- **A friend's width fits within her slots** (planned). nova-config refuses a friend width larger than her slots and names both values, so one-shot lanes cannot silently halve the friend's available capacity. From: dogfood 2026-10-10: one-shot friend at width 32 with 16 slots.
- **No friend runs in batch mode** (in-progress). A friend's delivery mode is one-shot always: nova-config refuses --mode batch, a stored batch row reads as one-shot (config.FriendMode, the reader nova-sprint's friend sync writes onto her roster row), and her daemon runs one card per lane. From: dogfood 2026-10-10: a friend row still mode=batch.
- **A one-shot friend's presence needs no session** (in-progress). A one-shot opencode friend has no long-lived session by design: her presence comes from the daemon and its lanes, never a growing session. Her session check goes in as a fresh turn of its own (opencode run with no --session), so a session that is full (past the model's context) or missing is never the reason she is down. From: the seat ledger v1.2.4-held-2026-10-10.md, two friends down after the adopt: one past the 260000-token context refused every turn, one with no opencode session in its directory.
- **A reader loop re-dials the sprint server after its restart** (in-progress). The sprint connection a reader beats and takes through is rebuilt after any error and backed off one second doubling to thirty (cmd/nova-swarm/sprintredial.go, tla/LoopRedial.tla), so a server restart drops the connection and the reader re-dials and keeps beating, instead of parking on the dead socket; fleet/loops.yml takes nova_loop_restart=<records> to restart a hung loop through the play, never by hand. From: measured 2026-10-11 01:05-01:20Z: after the v1.2.6 adopt every Linux reader loop stopped at its last connection-refused line while the member loops on the same hosts recovered, 24 reads waited with 0 reading and the server raised cannot ask (0 free readers) until each reader unit was restarted by hand.
- **Friend daemons follow the adopted release automatically** (in-progress). When the adopted build for a line changes, each friend host installs it through the play and proves its lanes, with no hand adopt per host. From: the owner 2026-10-10: what else is manual that should be automatic from the machine.

## v1.2.8 (planned)

The fleet-install fixes found while dogfooding v1.2.5 and later.

- **Every installed tool is checked against the release's bytes** (in-progress). After the install and the friends' reinstall, tools.yml lists each machine's bin directory with the sha256 of every file and compares it with the platform's SHA256SUMS; a tool built or copied on the machine, which prints the release's version and holds another toolchain's bytes, refuses the play (TOOLS REFUSED step=identity) and is named. --check says WOULD-REPLACE and refuses nothing. fleet/tools_test.go pins the check and that no task compiles a tool. From: dogfood 2026-10-10: after the v1.2.5 adopt one machine's nova-friend reported go1.27.1 while every other tool reported go1.26.6.

## v1.2.9 (planned)

A worker card whose last turn is a question ends as asked instead of holding its slot.

- **End a card as asked when its last turn is a question** (planned). A headless card whose last turn asks the user a question ends at once as asked instead of holding its slot to the deadline. From: issue #2548.
- **Adopt waits only for agents it stopped and dry-runs honestly** (shipped). The adopt window waits only for the agents the adopt itself stopped, and its dry run reports what each step would do instead of saying would for every step. From: card from the sprint store (2026-10-10).
- **Idle-reaped cards report their real cause and are not wrongly reaped** (planned). A reaped card reports a wall refusal that names nothing, and the harness shell cap silenced working cards. The verdict states idle reaping and the idle watch accounts for the shell cap. From: issue #2157; issue #2158; issue #2577; issue #2579; issue #2585.
- **A HOLD report with zero findings is malformed** (planned). A verdict of HOLD cannot have no findings, so the result check classes it as malformed. From: PR #4635.
- **Release adopt does not trust a partial release directory** (planned). A killed transfer leaves a partial release dir that the next adopt treats as complete. Adopt verifies completeness or uses a temporary dir renamed at the end. From: issue #1981.
- **The dispatcher releases a slot lease by its own id** (planned). Release removes every lease with the same owner and label. It releases only the one lease it took. From: issue #1582.
- **CI runs on card PRs are not cancelled under load** (planned). CI runs at the head of card PRs are cancelled mid-job when many PRs open together; the concurrency rule is fixed so each head gets one full run. From: issue #2795.
- **A cancelled workflow run counts as red for revert-on-red** (in-progress). Revert-on-red treats cancelled runs as failures so a cold-cache cancellation does not leave a bad main. From: PR #4600.
- **nova-swarm doctor checks the running executable, not only PATH** (planned). The launch preflight refuses a new binary found on PATH but passes the same binary by absolute path. It checks the executable that is actually running. From: issue #3469.
- **A limited inception route takes the global rate budget on every request** (shipped). A fleet member launches with --model only, so the job's generated opencode config named no baseURL for inception and the budget proxy never opened: a limited route's requests took no per-request budget. When a budget server is named, inception's entry is now given its API base from the providers table (https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1), the proxy opens in front of it and the harness is pointed at the proxy; the harness's own header and request timeouts are turned off on that route so a request waiting on its budget stalls and is never aborted. A route with no limit is unchanged; deepseek is not seeded. From: the card tmp/next-sprint-cards/inception-behind-the-limiter-proxy.md (the seat, 2026-10-11 ~02:55Z: the first Mercury 3 take on a limited route logged that inception had no http baseURL and the rpm bucket stayed at in_use=0).
